text: Dér Gréine is an Irish and Scottish heroine or goddess. Her name means 'Tear of the Sun'. She may have been a goddess first. She was the daughter of the sun deity or of the sun itself. In Ireland she was the daughter of a king. The king gave her to the hero Laoghaire mac Crimthann. This gift was the reward for his service to the king. Laoghaire had killed the fierce giant Goll Mac Morna. In Scotland a different story survives. She was held captive in the Land of Big Women. A young man named Brian freed her. Brian is a common folktale name. The Cailleach helped him. She was in disguise as a fox. As they escaped, the Cailleach sacrificed herself. Her death let Dér Gréine and Brian return safely.
objective: Describe Dér Gréine as the 'Tear of the Sun', an Irish and Scottish heroine or goddess.
